title: Compatibility layer parity: embeddings & rerank endpoints, error codes, and pagination semantics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As part of the compatibility layer work for the Core API, we need parity between legacy endpoints and the new unified endpoints for embeddings and reranking. Customers and downstream SDKs expect consistent pagination semantics and stable, documented error codes. Mismatches cause SDK breakage, incorrect rate-limiting behavior, and increased support burden.

Scope: Align behavior across: (1) embeddings endpoints (legacy /v1/embeddings vs new /v2/embeddings-compatible), (2) rerank endpoints (batch rerank vs stream-based rerank), and (3) shared error codes and pagination semantics for both endpoints. This ticket covers API contract, server-side behavior, SDK compatibility shims, docs, and a staged rollout plan. Implementation is expected to be server-side primarily with small SDK toggles.

Goals: Ensure backward-compatible behavior for customers that rely on older pagination and error semantics; provide a single compatibility layer flag for the console and SDK to toggle; unify error codes to the canonical list used by other Core APIs; document migration steps and provide a short grace period where both behaviors are supported.

Non-goals: Changes to embeddings vector formats, algorithmic rerank scoring, or performance optimizations beyond what is required for parity. Those remain in separate runtime performance tickets.

Acceptance criteria: 1) New compatibility layer returns identical pagination tokens and page sizes as legacy endpoints for same requests. 2) Error codes for rate limit, auth, payload validation, and server failures match canonical error list. 3) SDK compatibility flags successfully toggle behavior for at least Python and JS SDKs. 4) Integration tests that assert parity pass in CI for both legacy and compatibility modes. 5) Public docs updated with behavioral matrix and migration guide.

Design notes and constraints: - Pagination: legacy embeddings used a next_cursor token that encoded shard+offset; new runtime prefers cursor-less offsets. The compatibility layer must translate next_cursor <-> runtime cursor without exposing internal shard info. Page size defaults must match legacy (default 50 for embeddings, 20 for rerank). - Error codes: create canonical mapping table: 409->409_CONFLICT (kept), 429->RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 401->UNAUTHORIZED, 422->INVALID_REQUEST, 500->INTERNAL_ERROR. Clients that parsed numeric-only codes must still get numeric codes but with stable string identifiers in the body. - Retries: Publish explicit guidance: idempotent embedding list fetches are safe to retry on 500 with exponential backoff up to 3 tries; rerank is not idempotent if using streaming partial-results, so retries for streaming must fail fast.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement server-side compatibility flag "compat_mode=legacy-parity" behind a feature flag. 2) Build translation middleware for cursor tokens and error payloads. 3) Add unit/integration tests in ENG repos and expose test endpoints in staging. 4) Release SDK toggles simultaneously with server. 5) Enable default for newly created accounts only; existing customers must opt-in for 30 days, then flip by default after communication.

Telemetry & success metrics: - Reduction in embedding/rerank related support tickets by 60% within 8 weeks of rollout. - Test pass rate: 100% regression tests for pagination & error mapping in CI. - SDK adoption: 90% of active SDK calls opt-in or pass compatibility checks within 30 days.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Token translation may leak internal shard topology if not carefully encoded. Mitigation: Use HMAC-signed opaque tokens that only the compatibility middleware can decode. - Risk: Clients depending on subtle timing differences (streamed rerank) may observe behavior changes. Mitigation: Keep streaming path absolutely unchanged; only alter non-streamed control-plane semantics. - Risk: Performance regression from middleware. Mitigation: Microbenchmark and include perf budget (<=2% tail latency increase) in rollout gating.

Docs & comms: Update Developer Guide, SDK migration page, and Console feature toggle page. Draft customer-facing email and support KB with migration steps and example curl/python/js snippets.

Next steps: 1) PM to confirm canonical error mapping. 2) ENG to design token encoding. 3) Assign task to SDK owners for toggles. 4) Draft migration guide and comms.
acceptance_criteria: Pagination tokens produced in compatibility mode are semantically identical to legacy tokens for all supported endpoints
Canonical error list is implemented and returned in bodies; numeric status codes preserved for HTTP clients
Python and JS SDKs include a compatibility flag that toggles behavior and documented examples
CI integration tests validate parity for embeddings and rerank in both modes
Public docs and migration guide published before rolling default change
